<!-- source: packages/session/README.md -->

# @miujs/session

> Signed-cookie or server-side sessions for MiuJS, with flash messages and same-origin CSRF protection.

`session()` puts a `Session` on `ctx.session` for every request. By default all session data lives in an HMAC-SHA256 signed cookie; pass a `store` to keep data on the server (memory, SQL via `@miujs/db`, Cloudflare KV or Redis) and put only the signed id in the cookie. It also blocks cross-site unsafe requests that carry the session cookie. Use it on its own for anonymous state (carts, flash notices), and put it before `auth()` from `@miujs/auth`, which needs it.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/session miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { session } from "@miujs/session";

const setName = route.post("/name", {
  body: t.object({ name: t.string() }),
  handler: ({ session, body }) => {
    session.set("name", body.name);
    session.flash("notice", "Saved");
    return { ok: true };
  },
});

const getName = route.get("/name", {
  handler: ({ session }) => ({
    name: session.get<string>("name") ?? null,
    notice: session.get<string>("notice") ?? null, // flash: readable on the next request only
  }),
});

export default miu({ name: "demo", plugins: [session()], routes: [setName, getName] });
```

Set `SESSION_SECRET` (32+ random characters) in the environment, or pass `session({ secret })`. In dev without a secret, a random one is generated per process (sessions reset on restart) and a warning is logged once. Outside dev a missing secret is an error.

## The session API

`ctx.session` has:

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | Session id. Stable until `regenerate()` or `destroy()`. |
| `get<T>(key)` | Read a value (or a flash value set on the previous request). |
| `set(key, value)` | Write a JSON-serializable value. |
| `delete(key)` | Remove a key. |
| `flash(key, value)` | Store a value readable only during the next request. |
| `regenerate()` | New id, same data. Call on login and privilege changes (prevents session fixation). |
| `destroy()` | Clear all data and expire the cookie. |

A `Set-Cookie` header is only sent when the session changed. Responses that set the cookie also get `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. Other plugins can read the session with `getSession(ctx)`, which returns `undefined` when `session()` is not installed.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { session } from "@miujs/session";

const login = route.post("/login", {
  handler: ({ session }) => {
    session.regenerate(); // new id after a privilege change
    session.set("userId", "u_1");
  },
});
const logout = route.post("/logout", { handler: ({ session }) => void session.destroy() });

export default miu({ plugins: [session({ secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET })], routes: [login, logout] });
```

## Server-side stores

With a store, the cookie holds only the signed session id, so data size is not limited by the 4 KB cookie limit and `destroy()` deletes the record on the server.

| Store | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `memorySessionStore()` | In-process. Lost on restart, not shared between instances. Dev and tests. |
| `dbSessionStore(database, { table? })` | A `miu_sessions` table (created on first use) in any `@miujs/db` database: SQLite locally, D1 on Workers. |
| `kvSessionStore(bindingOrName)` | Cloudflare KV. Pass the binding, or its name to read it from `ctx.env` per request. Keys are prefixed `miu_session:`. |
| `redisSessionStore(client, { prefix? })` | Redis, expired by Redis (`SET ... PX`) and checked on read. Default prefix `miu:session:`. `bunRedis()` from `@miujs/cache` satisfies the client type. |

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu } from "miujs";
import { sqlite } from "@miujs/db";
import { dbSessionStore, memorySessionStore, session } from "@miujs/session";

const dev = miu({ plugins: [session({ store: memorySessionStore() })] });
const prod = miu({ plugins: [session({ store: dbSessionStore(sqlite("app.db")), maxAge: 24 * 3600 })] });

export { dev, prod };
```

Expired records are rejected on read by every store. Without a store (the default), logout cannot revoke a cookie that was copied elsewhere before it expired; use a server store if that matters.

## CSRF protection

With `csrf: true` (the default), a `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` that carries the session cookie must prove it came from this site:

- If `Origin` is present, its host must equal the request host or be in `trustedOrigins`.
- Otherwise `Referer` must match the same way.
- With neither header, the request is rejected (403 `MIU_E_CSRF`).

Requests without the session cookie (for example API clients using `Authorization: Bearer`) are not checked. `GET` is never checked.

Route tags change this:

- `csrf-exempt`: skip the check (webhooks).
- `csrf-always`: check even without a cookie (sign-in forms, against login CSRF). A browser request is rejected when `Origin`/`Referer` is cross-site or `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`; clients that send none of these headers (curl, servers) are allowed. `@miujs/auth` tags its login, register and logout routes this way.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { session } from "@miujs/session";

const webhook = route.post("/hooks/stripe", { tags: ["csrf-exempt"], handler: () => "ok" });
const signIn = route.post("/sign-in", { tags: ["csrf-always"], handler: () => "ok" });

export default miu({
  plugins: [session({ trustedOrigins: ["https://admin.example.com"] })],
  routes: [webhook, signIn],
});
```

## Cookie and secret details

- Cookie value: without a store, `base64url(JSON).signature`; with a store, `id.signature`. Signature is HMAC-SHA256, base64url.
- Defaults: name `miu_session`, `Max-Age` 7 days, `Path=/`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Secure` except on `http://localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`.
- Secrets shorter than 32 characters fail with `MIU_E_SESSION_SECRET_WEAK`.
- Rotation: pass an array. The first secret signs new cookies; all of them verify.
- Tampered, foreign-secret, malformed or expired cookies are ignored (the request gets a fresh session) and the bad cookie is expired.
- A cookie session larger than about 4 KB fails with `MIU_E_SESSION_TOO_LARGE` instead of being silently dropped by the browser.
- `inspect()` reports the store, cookie name, max age, CSRF setting and trusted origins, never the secret.

## Options

`session(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | `string \| string[]` | `env.SESSION_SECRET` | HMAC secret, 32+ characters. An array rotates: first signs, all verify. |
| `store` | `SessionStore` | none (data in the signed cookie) | Server-side store. |
| `maxAge` | `number` | `604800` (7 days) | Lifetime in seconds. |
| `cookieName` | `string` | `"miu_session"` | Cookie name. |
| `secure` | `boolean` | `true`, except for `http://localhost` | `Secure` cookie attribute. |
| `sameSite` | `"Lax" \| "Strict" \| "None"` | `"Lax"` | `SameSite` cookie attribute. |
| `httpOnly` | `boolean` | `true` | `HttpOnly` cookie attribute. |
| `domain` | `string` | none | `Domain` cookie attribute. |
| `path` | `string` | `"/"` | `Path` cookie attribute. |
| `trustedOrigins` | `string[]` | `[]` | Extra origins allowed to send unsafe requests with the cookie. |
| `csrf` | `boolean` | `true` | Same-origin check on unsafe methods. |
| `onWarning` | `(message: string) => void` | request logger | Where dev-mode warnings go. |

Store options: `dbSessionStore(database, { table })` (default `"miu_sessions"`), `redisSessionStore(client, { prefix })` (default `"miu:session:"`).

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, `session()` shows a **Sessions** section:

- **Status**: storage (`cookie` or the store kind), active sessions (memory and `dbSessionStore`; capped at 10000+; KV, Redis and cookies say they cannot count), max age, whether a secret is configured (never the secret itself; a random dev secret is flagged) and whether the CSRF check is on.
- **Settings**: `maxAge` in seconds (60 s to 400 days). Applies to sessions written from then on.
- **Active sessions** list (memory and `dbSessionStore`; paged, search = exact user id). Session ids are secrets, so rows show only a 12-character SHA-256 prefix; each row carries an encrypted reference (AES-GCM, key derived from the session secret) for the **revoke** row action.
- **Action** `revokeUser` (danger): delete every session whose `userId` (what `@miujs/auth` stores) matches. Memory and `dbSessionStore` only.

Cookie sessions cannot be listed or revoked one by one: rotate `SESSION_SECRET` to sign everyone out. KV and Redis stores cannot be listed or searched by user.

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_SESSION_SECRET_MISSING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_secret_missing): no secret outside dev. Set `SESSION_SECRET`.
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_SECRET_WEAK`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_secret_weak): a secret is shorter than 32 characters.
- [`MIU_E_CSRF`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_csrf): 403, cross-site unsafe request with the session cookie (or on a `csrf-always` route).
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_TOO_LARGE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_too_large): cookie session over ~4 KB. Store less or use a server store.
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_KV_MISSING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_kv_missing): `kvSessionStore("NAME")` but no such KV binding in `env`.
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_TABLE_INVALID`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_table_invalid): `dbSessionStore` table name is not letters, digits and underscores.
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_REDIS_CLIENT`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_redis_client): `redisSessionStore` got something without `get`/`set`/`del`.
- [`MIU_E_SESSION_REDIS`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_session_redis): a Redis command failed.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

- `SESSION_SECRET` is read from `env` per request; set it with `wrangler secret put SESSION_SECRET`.
- The default cookie store needs no bindings.
- `kvSessionStore("SESSIONS")` reads the KV namespace from `env` per request and declares `kv: ["SESSIONS"]` for `miu deploy cloudflare`. KV's minimum TTL is 60 seconds, so TTLs are raised to at least 60; expiry is also checked on read.
- `dbSessionStore(d1("DB"))` declares `d1: ["DB"]`.
- Passing a binding object instead of a name works too, but declares nothing.

# @miujs/db

> D1-compatible SQL for MiuJS: one `Database` interface over Cloudflare D1 and local bun:sqlite, with migrations, introspection and optional Drizzle ORM.

`@miujs/db` adds `ctx.db`, a small D1-shaped interface (`prepare`/`bind`/`first`/`all`/`run`/`raw`, `batch`, `exec`). The same code runs on a Cloudflare D1 binding and, locally, on `bun:sqlite`. It applies SQL migrations once per database, reads schemas back with `introspect()`, and, through the `@miujs/db/drizzle` entry point, decorates `ctx.orm` with Drizzle. The `@miujs/db/postgres` entry adds Postgres (Hyperdrive on Workers, a pool elsewhere) with Drizzle and postgres.js; see [Postgres](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/db/README.md#postgres). MySQL is not supported; use Drizzle directly.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/db miujs
bun add drizzle-orm   # optional, for @miujs/db/drizzle and @miujs/db/postgres
bun add postgres      # optional, only for @miujs/db/postgres
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet). `drizzle-orm` (`>=0.45.0 <1`) is an optional peer dependency used only by the `@miujs/db/drizzle` and `@miujs/db/postgres` subpaths, and `postgres` (postgres.js, `>=3.4.4 <4`) only by `@miujs/db/postgres`; `@miujs/db` itself imports neither.

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { db } from "@miujs/db";

const migrations = [{ id: "001_notes", sql: "CREATE TABLE notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT NOT NULL);" }];

export const addNote = route.post("/notes", {
  body: t.object({ body: t.string() }),
  handler: async ({ body, db }) => {
    const r = await db.prepare("INSERT INTO notes (body) VALUES (?)").bind(body.body).run();
    return { id: r.meta.last_row_id };
  },
});

export const listNotes = route.get("/notes", {
  handler: async ({ db }) => {
    const { results } = await db.prepare("SELECT id, body FROM notes ORDER BY id").all<{ id: number; body: string }>();
    return { notes: results };
  },
});

const app = miu({ name: "notes", routes: [addNote, listNotes], plugins: [db({ migrations })] });
export default app;
```

With no `database`, `db()` uses `sqlite(":memory:")` on Bun and `d1("DB")` on Workers. Migrations run once per database before its first request.

## The Database interface

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { sqlite } from "@miujs/db";

const database = sqlite("./data/app.sqlite");
await database.exec("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, body TEXT, done INTEGER)");

const insert = database.prepare("INSERT INTO notes (body, done) VALUES (?, ?)");
await database.batch([insert.bind("a", false), insert.bind("b", true)]);

const first = await database.prepare("SELECT body FROM notes WHERE id = ?").bind(1).first<string>("body");
const { results } = await database.prepare("SELECT body FROM notes ORDER BY id").all<{ body: string }>();
const rows = await database.prepare("SELECT id, body FROM notes").raw({ columnNames: true });
console.log(first, results, rows);
```

- `bind()` returns a new statement. Booleans become `1`/`0` like D1; `undefined` is rejected (`MIU_E_DB_BIND_UNDEFINED`), pass `null` instead.
- `first()` returns a row, `first(column)` one column, or `null`.
- `batch()` runs statements in one transaction.
- `exec()` runs a raw script; `splitSql()` splits it on `;`, keeping trigger bodies and quoted text intact.
- `sqlite(path)` opens the file on first use with `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`. Bun only.

## Migrations

`migrate(database, migrations)` applies migrations not yet recorded in `_miu_migrations`, in order, each in one transaction with its bookkeeping row, and returns the applied ids. `migrateOnce` does the same at most once per (database, list) in this isolate; the plugin uses it.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { loadMigrations, migrate, migrationsFromGlob, sqlite } from "@miujs/db";

const database = sqlite();
const fromDisk = await loadMigrations("./migrations"); // 0001_init.sql, 0002_users.sql, ...
const applied = await migrate(database, fromDisk);
console.log(applied);

const bundled = migrationsFromGlob({ "0001_init.sql": "CREATE TABLE t (x INTEGER);" });
await migrate(database, bundled);
```

- `loadMigrations(dir)` reads `NNNN_name.sql` files ordered by number; the id is the file name without `.sql`. Bun, Node and Deno only.
- `migrationsFromGlob(files)` takes `{ path: sqlText }` (or `{ default: sqlText }` modules), for Workers.
- A failed migration is rolled back; earlier ones stay applied. Never rename an applied migration.

## Introspection

`introspect(database)` returns a `SchemaDescription` (tables, columns, primary keys, indexes, foreign keys) on D1 or `sqlite()`, skipping internal tables. `generateDrizzleSchema(desc)` turns it into Drizzle `schema.ts` source, and `tableSql` / `createTableSql` / `createIndexSql` render DDL from a description.

## Drizzle

Import `@miujs/db/drizzle` (needs `drizzle-orm`). `db({ drizzle: { schema } })` decorates `ctx.orm`; `drizzleFor(database, options)` works outside requests; `drizzle(ctx)` returns `ctx.orm` or Drizzle over `ctx.db`.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { eq } from "drizzle-orm";
import { integer, sqliteTable, text } from "drizzle-orm/sqlite-core";
import { sqlite } from "@miujs/db";
import { drizzleFor } from "@miujs/db/drizzle";

const users = sqliteTable("users", {
  id: integer("id").primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  email: text("email").notNull().unique(),
  admin: integer("admin", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(false),
});

const database = sqlite();
await database.exec("CREATE TABLE users (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, admin INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0)");

const orm = drizzleFor(database, { schema: { users } });
await orm.insert(users).values({ email: "alice@x" });
const admins = await orm.select().from(users).where(eq(users.admin, true));
console.log(admins);
```

To type `ctx.orm`, register the schema once:

```ts
declare module "@miujs/db/drizzle" {
  interface DrizzleRegister { schema: typeof schema }
}
```

The subpath also exports `tableFromSchema(name, t.object(...), { primaryKey, indexes, references, casing })`, which builds a Drizzle table and its `CREATE TABLE` SQL from a MiuJS schema; `schemaFromTable(table, { mode })` for the reverse; and `describeTable` / `diffSchema(current, tables, { ignore })` to compute migration SQL against an introspected database.

## Options

`db(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `database` | `Database \| DatabaseRef` | `d1("DB")` on Workers, `sqlite(":memory:")` elsewhere | The database, or a D1 binding name via `d1("NAME")`. |
| `migrations` | `Migration[]` | none | Applied once per database before its first request. |
| `drizzle` | `{ schema?, logger?, casing? }` | none | Also set `ctx.orm`. Needs `drizzle-orm`. |

`drizzleFor(database, options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `Record<string, unknown>` | none | Tables and relations for `orm.query.<table>`. |
| `logger` | `boolean \| Logger` | none | Drizzle query logging. |
| `casing` | `"snake_case" \| "camelCase"` | none | Drizzle column name casing. |

`sqlite(path)`: `path` defaults to `":memory:"`.

## Postgres

`@miujs/db/postgres` (needs `postgres` and `drizzle-orm`) gives each request `ctx.orm` (Drizzle over postgres.js) and `ctx.sql` (the postgres.js client). On Cloudflare Workers it creates a client per request from a Hyperdrive binding and closes it after the response; on Bun, Node and Deno it keeps one pool from `DATABASE_URL` that `app.close()` closes. `migratePostgres(sql, migrations)` applies the same `NNNN_name.sql` files, and `fromPgError(err)` maps constraint errors to 409/400 MiuErrors.

```ts
import { pg } from "@miujs/db/postgres";

const database = pg({ schema, hyperdriveId: "<id>" }); // DATABASE_URL off Workers, env.HYPERDRIVE on Workers
const app = miu({ plugins: [database], routes: [route.get("/n", { handler: async (ctx) => (await ctx.sql`SELECT 1 AS n`)[0] })] });
```

The rest of this package (`db()`, `ctx.db`, `migrate()`, `introspect()`, `diffSchema()`, `tableFromSchema()`) and `@miujs/admin` resources are SQLite/D1 only. Setup, Hyperdrive, pooling, transactions, migrations, testing with PGlite and what is and is not tested: [docs/postgres.md](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/postgres.md). Example: [examples/postgres](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/examples/postgres).

## In @miujs/admin

`db()` has a management section (`manage()`), shown by `@miujs/admin`:

- **Status**: adapter (`sqlite`, or `d1 (binding DB)`), tables with row counts (first 50 tables; counts stop at 10,000 so a big table is never fully scanned), applied migrations (every plugin's, from `_miu_migrations`) and pending ones from `db({ migrations })`.
- **Migrations list** (filter applied / pending).
- **Apply pending migrations** (dangerous; only when `db({ migrations })` is set): runs `migrate()` with those migrations, each in its own transaction. Running it again does nothing.

There is no way to run arbitrary SQL from the admin, on purpose.

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_DB_BINDING_MISSING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_binding_missing): no D1 binding with that name in `env`.
- [`MIU_E_DB_UNSUPPORTED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_unsupported): `sqlite()` off Bun, or `loadMigrations()` on Workers.
- [`MIU_E_DB_BIND_UNDEFINED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_bind_undefined): `undefined` passed to `bind()`.
- [`MIU_E_DB_MIGRATION_FAILED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_migration_failed): a migration's SQL failed and was rolled back.
- [`MIU_E_DB_MIGRATION_NAME`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_migration_name) / [`MIU_E_DB_MIGRATION_DUPLICATE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_migration_duplicate): a `.sql` file without a number, or two sharing one.
- [`MIU_E_DB_MIGRATIONS_DIR`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_migrations_dir): the migrations directory cannot be read.
- [`MIU_E_DB_MIGRATION_INVALID`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_migration_invalid): a `migrationsFromGlob` value is not text.
- [`MIU_E_DB_DRIZZLE_MISSING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_drizzle_missing): `db({ drizzle })` could not load `drizzle-orm`.
- [`MIU_E_DB_MISSING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_missing): `drizzle(ctx)` with no `ctx.db`.
- [`MIU_E_DB_SCHEMA`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_db_schema): invalid `tableFromSchema` options.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

On Workers the default database is the D1 binding `DB`; `d1("NAME")` picks another, resolved from `ctx.env` per request. The plugin reports the binding to `miu deploy cloudflare`.

```toml
[[d1_databases]]
binding = "DB"
database_name = "<name>"
database_id = "<id>"

# to bundle migrations as text for migrationsFromGlob
rules = [{ type = "Text", globs = ["**/*.sql"] }]
```

When bundling with `db({ drizzle })`, add `import "@miujs/db/drizzle";` to your entry so the bundler includes Drizzle. `sqlite()` is Bun only and `loadMigrations()` needs a filesystem (Bun, Node, Deno); on Workers use `d1()` and `migrationsFromGlob()`.

<!-- source: packages/cache/README.md -->

# @miujs/cache

> Key/value cache for MiuJS with TTLs, tag invalidation and `remember()`, backed by memory, Cloudflare KV or Redis.

`@miujs/cache` adds `ctx.cache` to every request. Values are JSON-serialized, reads return fresh copies, and `remember()` shares one computation between concurrent callers for the same key. With no options it uses an in-process LRU locally and the KV namespace bound as `CACHE` on Cloudflare Workers. Use it to cache expensive reads, API responses or computed data.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/cache miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { cache } from "@miujs/cache";

let hits = 0;

export const counter = route.get("/count/:id", {
  params: t.object({ id: t.string() }),
  handler: async ({ params, cache }) => {
    return cache.remember(`count:${params.id}`, 60, async () => ({ computed: ++hits }));
  },
});

const app = miu({ name: "cache-demo", routes: [counter], plugins: [cache()] });
export default app;
```

`cache()` with no options uses `memoryStore()` (1000 entries) locally, and `kvStore` over `env.CACHE` on Workers when that binding exists.

## The client

`ctx.cache` (and `createCache(store)`) is a `CacheClient`:

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get<T>(key)` | Value or `undefined`. Corrupt entries read as a miss. |
| `set(key, value, { ttl?, tags? })` | `ttl` in seconds; omit to keep until evicted or deleted. |
| `delete(key)` | Removes one key. |
| `remember<T>(key, ttlSeconds, fn)` | Returns the cached value or runs `fn`, caches its result and returns it. Errors and `undefined` are not cached. |
| `invalidateTag(tag)` | Deletes every key that was `set` with this tag. |

Tag indexes are stored under keys starting with `TAG_PREFIX` (`"__miu:tag:"`); do not use that prefix for your own keys. An index drops keys that expired or were deleted once it has doubled in size, and when all of its keys have a TTL it expires a minute after the last one, so tags that are never invalidated do not pile up in Redis or KV.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { createCache, memoryStore } from "@miujs/cache";

const cache = createCache(memoryStore({ maxEntries: 500 }));

await cache.set("user:1", { name: "Mia" }, { ttl: 300, tags: ["users"] });
const user = await cache.get<{ name: string }>("user:1");
console.log(user?.name);

await cache.invalidateTag("users");
console.log(await cache.get("user:1")); // undefined
```

Use `createCache(store)` outside requests (jobs, scripts). Clients over the same store share in-flight `remember()` calls.

## Stores

### Memory

`memoryStore({ maxEntries, now })` is an in-process LRU with TTLs. Each process (and each Workers isolate) has its own copy, so it is not shared between servers.

### Cloudflare KV

`kvStore(binding)` takes a KV binding or its name. A name is resolved from `ctx.env` on each request, and a missing binding fails only the requests that use the cache (`MIU_E_CACHE_BINDING`).

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu } from "miujs";
import { cache, kvStore } from "@miujs/cache";

export default miu({ name: "kv-cache", plugins: [cache({ store: kvStore("MY_KV") })] });
```

Notes:

- TTLs under 60 seconds are raised to 60 (`KV_MIN_TTL`, KV's minimum).
- KV is eventually consistent (up to about 60 s across locations), so `delete` and `invalidateTag` may take that long to be seen everywhere, and tag indexes written from two locations at once can lose a key.

### Redis

`redisStore(client, { prefix })` stores entries in Redis and lets Redis expire them (`SET ... PX`). The client is any `RedisLike`:

- `bunRedis(url?, options?)` wraps Bun's built-in client. `url` defaults to `REDIS_URL`, then `VALKEY_URL`, then `redis://localhost:6379`. Bun only.
- `redisFromCommand(send)` adapts anything that can send a raw command (node-redis `sendCommand`, ioredis `call`, ...).

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu } from "miujs";
import { bunRedis, cache, redisStore } from "@miujs/cache";

const store = redisStore(bunRedis(), { prefix: "myapp:cache:" });

export default miu({ name: "redis-cache", plugins: [cache({ store })] });
```

With another client:

```ts
import { createClient } from "redis";
import { redisFromCommand, redisStore } from "@miujs/cache";

const client = createClient({ url: process.env.REDIS_URL });
await client.connect();
const store = redisStore(redisFromCommand((cmd, args) => client.sendCommand([cmd, ...args])));
```

`RedisLike` avoids MULTI and EVAL, so Valkey, Dragonfly, KeyDB and Upstash work. The same client also serves `redisQueue` from `@miujs/queue`. Its `scan` method is optional: without it the cache works the same but the admin cannot list or purge keys by prefix.

### Custom stores

A `CacheStore` moves strings: `name`, `get(key)`, `set(key, value, { ttl })`, `delete(key)`, and optionally `size()`, `bytes()`, `scan(query)`, `clear()`, `forEnv(env)` and `inspect()`.

## Options

`cache(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | `CacheStore` | `memoryStore()`; on Workers `kvStore(env.CACHE)` when bound | Where entries live. |

`memoryStore(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxEntries` | `number` | `1000` | Entries kept before the least recently used is evicted. |
| `now` | `() => number` | `Date.now` | Clock in milliseconds, for tests. |

`redisStore(client, options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prefix` | `string` | `"miu:cache:"` | Prepended to every key. `""` for none. |

`set(key, value, options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ttl` | `number` | none | Seconds until the entry expires. Must be positive. |
| `tags` | `string[]` | `[]` | Tags for `invalidateTag`. |

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, the plugin shows a **Cache** section:

- **Status**: store name, entries and total size (memory store; `null` with a hint on KV and Redis, which cannot count cheaply), hits, misses and hit rate counted by this instance since it started.
- **Keys** list (paged, search = key prefix, values are never shown): memory store, KV when the binding has `list()` (real Cloudflare bindings do), and Redis when the client has `scan` (`bunRedis()` and `redisFromCommand()` do). On Redis the list walks `SCAN cursor MATCH <prefix>* COUNT 250` over the store's own prefix only (glob characters in the search are matched literally); size and expiry show as empty. With a `RedisLike` that lacks the optional `scan`, the list explains that it cannot list keys. Row action: delete.
- **Actions**: `deleteKey`, `invalidateTag`, `purgePrefix` (danger) and `purgeAll` (danger). Purges need a store that can list keys and delete at most 1000 keys per run; the result says when more remain. `purgeAll` on the memory store clears it at once; on Redis it deletes the keys under the store's prefix, never other keys in the database.

Custom stores can opt in by implementing `scan({ prefix, cursor, limit })`, `clear()` and `bytes()`.

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_CACHE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_config): invalid store options (e.g. `maxEntries`, Redis client, prefix).
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_KEY`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_key): a key or tag is not a non-empty string.
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_TTL`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_ttl): `ttl` is not a positive number of seconds.
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_VALUE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_value): the value is not JSON-serializable (`undefined`, BigInt, cycles).
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_BINDING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_binding): the named KV binding is missing from `env`.
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_REDIS`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_redis): a Redis command failed.
- [`MIU_E_CACHE_REDIS_RUNTIME`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_cache_redis_runtime): `bunRedis()` called outside Bun.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

With no `store`, the plugin uses the KV namespace bound as `CACHE` (`DEFAULT_KV_BINDING`) and falls back to memory if it is absent. With `kvStore("NAME")`, the plugin reports the binding to `miu deploy cloudflare`.

```toml
[[kv_namespaces]]
binding = "CACHE"
id = "<namespace-id>"
```

`memoryStore()` works on Workers but is per isolate. `bunRedis()` is Bun only; on Workers use `kvStore`, or `redisFromCommand` over an HTTP Redis client.

## Links

- [Getting started guide](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/guide.md)
- [Error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md)
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/AGENTS.md)
- [Source](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/cache/src)
- [Tests](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/cache/test)
- Related: [@miujs/queue](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/queue/README.md), [@miujs/ratelimit](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/ratelimit/README.md), [@miujs/db](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/db/README.md)

<!-- source: packages/queue/README.md -->

# @miujs/queue

> Background jobs and cron schedules for MiuJS, with retries, backoff and dead letters, on memory, SQLite, Redis or Cloudflare Queues.

`@miujs/queue` adds `ctx.queue.dispatch(job, input, { delay })`. Jobs are declared with `defineJob`, take a `t` schema for input, and are retried with backoff when they throw. Cron schedules dispatch a job on a 5-field UTC expression. With no adapter it runs jobs in-process on Bun, Deno and Node, and uses Cloudflare Queues (binding `JOBS`) on Workers.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/queue miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { defineJob, queue } from "@miujs/queue";

export const sendEmail = defineJob("send-email", {
  input: t.object({ to: t.string() }),
  retries: 3,
  run: async ({ input, attempt, log }) => {
    log.info("sending", { to: input.to, attempt });
  },
});

export const signup = route.post("/signup", {
  body: t.object({ email: t.string() }),
  handler: async ({ body, queue }) => {
    const { id } = await queue.dispatch(sendEmail, { to: body.email });
    return { queued: id };
  },
});

const app = miu({ name: "queue-demo", routes: [signup], plugins: [queue({ jobs: [sendEmail] })] });
export default app;
```

`dispatch` validates the input against the job's schema and resolves once the message is accepted, not when it has run. Pass `{ delay: seconds }` to wait before the first attempt.

## Jobs

A job's `run` receives `{ input, attempt, maxAttempts, id, job, log, env, dispatch }`. `attempt` is 1 on the first try; `id` is stable across retries. `dispatch` enqueues another job.

- A thrown error retries the job after its `backoff` until `retries` are used up, then the message becomes a dead letter.
- `backoff: "exponential"` waits 5 s, 10 s, 20 s, ... up to 1 h; a number is a fixed delay in seconds.
- Invalid input and unknown jobs are never retried.

## Schedules

`schedule(cron, job, input?)` runs `job` whenever the expression matches. Expressions have 5 fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week), support `*`, numbers, `a-b`, `a,b` and `/n`, and are matched in UTC. Scheduled jobs are registered automatically.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, t } from "miujs";
import { defineJob, queue, schedule } from "@miujs/queue";

const report = defineJob("daily-report", {
  input: t.object({ day: t.string() }),
  backoff: 30,
  run: async ({ input, log }) => {
    log.info("report", { day: input.day });
  },
});

const jobs = queue({ schedules: [schedule("0 6 * * *", report, { day: "today" })] });

export default miu({ name: "cron-demo", plugins: [jobs] });
```

On Bun, Deno and Node the adapter fires schedules itself. On Workers they run from Cron Triggers.

## Adapters

### Memory (default off Workers)

`memoryQueue({ concurrency, clock, maxDeadLetters })` runs jobs in this process; they are lost if it exits. It keeps the newest `maxDeadLetters` (default 1000) dead letters in memory, and `drain()` resolves once nothing is queued, running or delayed. With `manualClock()`, `drain()` skips delays and backoff, which makes job tests fast. Its timers (schedules, delays, retry backoff) are unref'd, so they never keep the process alive on their own: a delayed job that has not run when the process exits is lost, like any in-process job. Use `sqliteQueue` or `redisQueue` when delayed jobs must survive.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { t } from "miujs";
import { defineJob, manualClock, memoryQueue, queue } from "@miujs/queue";

let failures = 0;
const flaky = defineJob("flaky", {
  input: t.object({}),
  retries: 1,
  run: () => {
    failures++;
    throw new Error("boom");
  },
});

const adapter = memoryQueue({ clock: manualClock() });
const q = queue({ jobs: [flaky], adapter });

await q.dispatch(flaky, {});
await adapter.drain();
console.log(failures, adapter.deadLetters.length); // 2 1
q.stop();
```

The plugin's own `dispatch(job, input, opts?, env?)` works outside requests (scripts, tests); `stop()` clears schedule and delay timers. `cancel(id)` (also `ctx.queue.cancel(id)`) removes a message that has not started, e.g. a delayed one, by the id `dispatch` returned; it resolves false when the message already ran or is running (memory, SQLite and Redis; Cloudflare Queues cannot cancel). `addSchedule(schedule(...))` and `removeSchedule(s)` change cron schedules at runtime: on Bun, Deno and Node the minute scheduler starts with the first schedule and stops with the last; on Workers a cron fires only if it is also a Cron Trigger in wrangler.toml.

### SQLite (Bun only)

`sqliteQueue(pathOrDatabase, options)` keeps jobs in a `bun:sqlite` file, so they survive restarts. Several processes on one machine can share the file. A job whose process dies is rerun after `visibilityTimeout`.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { Database } from "bun:sqlite";
import { t } from "miujs";
import { defineJob, queue, sqliteQueue } from "@miujs/queue";

const job = defineJob("resize", { input: t.object({ file: t.string() }), run: () => {} });
const adapter = sqliteQueue(new Database(":memory:"), { table: "jobs", concurrency: 2 });
const q = queue({ jobs: [job], adapter });

await q.dispatch(job, { file: "a.png" });
console.log(await adapter.stats()); // { pending, delayed, inflight, deadLetters }
adapter.close();
```

Pass a path (`sqliteQueue("./data/jobs.sqlite")`) to let the queue open and own the database. Dead letters and schedule locks use `<table>_dead` and `<table>_once`.

### Redis

`redisQueue(client, options)` shares one queue between servers. `bunRedis()` and `redisFromCommand()` from `@miujs/cache` provide the client.

```ts
import { bunRedis } from "@miujs/cache";
import { queue, redisQueue } from "@miujs/queue";

queue({ jobs, adapter: redisQueue(bunRedis(), { concurrency: 4 }) });
```

SQLite and Redis adapters are `DurableQueue`s: `drain()`, `stop()`, `close()`, `listDeadLetters()` and `stats()`. Jobs receive the process env, not the dispatching request's env. Their poll, schedule and lease-renewal timers are unref'd, so an idle app exits without calling `stop()`. After `stop()` a job that is still running finishes, but the worker claims nothing more; after `close()` the queue never reopens its database. Dead letters are kept in storage (`<table>_dead`, or the `dead` list in Redis) until you delete them, so prune them periodically if jobs fail often.

### Cloudflare Queues (default on Workers)

`cloudflareQueue({ binding, queue })` sends `{ id, job, input }` to the producer binding and runs the consumer through `app.on("queue")`. See [Cloudflare Workers](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/queue/README.md#cloudflare-workers).

## Options

`queue(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `jobs` | `JobDef[]` | `[]` | Jobs this queue can run. |
| `schedules` | `Schedule[]` | `[]` | Cron schedules; their jobs are registered automatically. |
| `adapter` | `QueueAdapter` | `memoryQueue()`; `cloudflareQueue()` on Workers | Queue backend. |

`defineJob(name, config)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `Schema` | required | `t` schema for the input; `t.object({})` for none. |
| `retries` | `number` | `3` | Retries after the first failed attempt. |
| `backoff` | `"exponential" \| number` | `"exponential"` | Delay before each retry (seconds when a number). |
| `run` | `(ctx) => unknown` | required | The job body. |

`memoryQueue(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `concurrency` | `number` | `1` | Jobs run at the same time. |
| `clock` | `Clock` | `realClock` | Time source; `manualClock()` in tests. |

`sqliteQueue` / `redisQueue` options:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `concurrency` | `number` | `1` | Jobs this process runs at the same time. |
| `visibilityTimeout` | `number` | `30` | Seconds a running job's lease lasts; renewed while it runs. |
| `pollInterval` | `number` | `1000` | Milliseconds between checks for due jobs. |
| `clock` | `Clock` | `realClock` | Time source. |
| `table` (SQLite) | `string` | `"miu_jobs"` | Table name. |
| `prefix` (Redis) | `string` | `"miu:queue:"` | Key prefix. |

`cloudflareQueue(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `binding` | `string` | `"JOBS"` | Producer binding name. |
| `queue` | `string` | all batches | Only consume batches from this queue name. |

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, the plugin shows a **Queue** section:

- **Status**: adapter, pending, delayed, running and dead-letter counts (memory, SQLite and Redis; Cloudflare Queues cannot be counted or listed from a Worker, so those stats are `null` with a hint pointing to the Cloudflare dashboard), whether this instance is paused, its concurrency, a **Jobs** table (retries, backoff, last run and result in this instance) and a **Schedules** table (cron, job, last fired in this instance).
- **Jobs** list (memory, SQLite, Redis), filtered by state (`pending`, `delayed`, `running`), paged by offset up to 10 000. Row action: `delete` (danger, only jobs that have not started).
- **Dead letters** list, newest first. Row actions: `retry` (queues the message again as attempt 1) and `delete` (danger). Both are idempotent: a second run says there is nothing to do. On Redis, retry/delete find a letter by id through a `deadid:<id>` index key wherever it is in the list; letters dead-lettered before that index existed (no migration needed) are looked for among the newest 10 000.
- **Actions**: `dispatch` (enqueue a job with JSON input, validated by its schema; internal `miu.*` jobs are refused), `runSchedule` (dispatch a schedule's job with its input now; pass `cron` when the job has several), and `pause` / `resume` (this instance only; jobs are still accepted, other instances keep running, a restart resumes).
- **Settings**: `concurrency` (1–1000), applied at once in this instance.

Job inputs are shown as compact JSON with secret-looking keys (`password`, `token`, `apiKey`, `secret`, ...) replaced by `[redacted]`. Custom adapters opt in by implementing the optional `QueueManagement` methods (`stats`, `listJobs`, `listDead`, `retryDead`, `deleteDead`, `pause`, `resume`, `setConcurrency`, ...); durable backends by implementing `jobs`, `deadPage` and `takeDead`.

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_VALIDATION`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_validation): job input does not match its schema.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_CONFIG`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_config): invalid job, adapter or option.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_CRON`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_cron): invalid cron expression.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_UNKNOWN_JOB`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_unknown_job): the job is not registered with this queue.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_JOB_DUPLICATE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_job_duplicate): two jobs share a name.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_DELAY`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_delay): `delay` is negative or too long (12 h on Cloudflare).
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_BINDING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_binding): the Cloudflare Queue binding is missing.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_timeout): a job's lease ran out with no attempts left.
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_RUNTIME`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_runtime): adapter used on an unsupported runtime (e.g. SQLite off Bun).
- [`MIU_E_QUEUE_SQLITE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_sqlite) / [`MIU_E_QUEUE_REDIS`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_queue_redis): a backend operation failed.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

On Workers the default adapter is `cloudflareQueue()` with producer and consumer binding `JOBS`. Successful messages are acked; failures call `retry({ delaySeconds })` with the job's backoff until its retries are used up. Set `max_retries` above your largest `retries` so Cloudflare does not give up first. Schedules run from Cron Triggers whose cron equals the schedule's.

```toml
[[queues.producers]]
binding = "JOBS"
queue = "<queue-name>"

[[queues.consumers]]
queue = "<queue-name>"
max_retries = 10

[triggers]
crons = ["0 6 * * *"]
```

`miu deploy cloudflare` reads the producer, consumer and crons from the plugin. `sqliteQueue` is Bun only and `memoryQueue` is per isolate; `redisQueue` needs a TCP Redis client, so use `cloudflareQueue` on Workers.

## Links

- [Getting started guide](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/guide.md)
- [Error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md)
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/AGENTS.md)
- [Source](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/queue/src)
- [Tests](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/queue/test)
- Related: [@miujs/cache](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/cache/README.md), [@miujs/db](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/db/README.md), [@miujs/ratelimit](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/packages/ratelimit/README.md)

<!-- source: packages/ratelimit/README.md -->

# @miujs/ratelimit

> Rules-based rate limiting for MiuJS with fixed, sliding and token-bucket algorithms, IETF RateLimit headers, and memory, KV, Durable Object, Cloudflare binding and Redis stores.

`@miujs/ratelimit` provides the `rateLimit()` plugin: each rule matches requests by route, path, method or tag, counts them per IP, user, API key or a function, and blocks with 429 `MIU_E_RATE_LIMITED` and `Retry-After` when the limit is reached. `limiter()` applies the same algorithms outside routes (WebSocket messages, jobs), and `asAuthLimiter()` lets `@miujs/auth` use any of these stores.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/ratelimit miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { rateLimit } from "@miujs/ratelimit";

const login = route.post("/auth/login", { name: "auth_login", handler: () => ({ ok: true }) });
const items = route.get("/api/items", { name: "items", handler: () => ({ items: [] }) });

const app = miu({
  name: "ratelimit-demo",
  routes: [login, items],
  plugins: [
    rateLimit({
      rules: [
        { name: "login", match: { route: "auth_login" }, limit: 10, window: "15m", by: "ip" },
        { name: "api", match: { path: "/api/*" }, limit: 100, window: "1m" },
      ],
    }),
  ],
});
export default app;
```

Responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` for the matching rule with the fewest requests left.

## Rules

- `match` takes `route` (route name), `path` (`/api/*` matches the path and everything below; `:param` and `*` match one segment), `method` and `tag`. Every given key must match; a list matches any of its entries. A rule without `match` applies to every request.
- `by` is `"ip"`, `"user"` (signed-in user, else IP), `"apiKey"` (`x-api-key` or `Authorization: Bearer`, hashed; else IP) or `(ctx) => string | null`. Returning `null` exempts the request.
- `window` is seconds or `"10s"`, `"1m"`, `"15m"`, `"1h"`, `"1d"`.
- Rules with `by: "user"` need `auth()` listed before `rateLimit()` in `plugins`; otherwise setup fails with `MIU_E_RATELIMIT_ORDER`.
- Behind a proxy, set `trustProxyHeader` (e.g. `"x-forwarded-for"`). The rightmost address is used. Never name a header clients can set directly.

### Algorithms

| Algorithm | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `"sliding"` (default) | Weighted sliding window over the current and previous window. |
| `"fixed"` | Counter reset at each window boundary. |
| `"token-bucket"` | Refills `limit` tokens per `window`; `burst` sets the capacity. |

## limiter() outside routes

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { limiter } from "@miujs/ratelimit";

const perPlayer = limiter({ limit: 20, window: "1s", algorithm: "token-bucket", burst: 40, name: "player" });

const result = await perPlayer.check("player:42");
if (!result.allowed) console.log(`retry in ${result.retryAfter}s`);

await perPlayer.reset("player:42");
```

`check(key, { env, cost })` returns the decision plus `retryAfter` (seconds, 0 when allowed) and `reset` (seconds until the window resets). On Workers pass `env` so binding-based stores can find their binding.

## Stores

| Store | Exact | Algorithms | Runtimes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `memoryStore({ maxKeys })` | per process | all | all (per isolate on Workers) |
| `redisStore(client, { prefix })` | yes | fixed, sliding | any with a Redis client |
| `kvStore(binding, { prefix })` | no (eventually consistent) | all | Workers |
| `durableObjectStore(binding)` | yes | all | Workers |
| `cloudflareBindingStore(binding, { limit, period })` | no (per location) | fixed, sliding; `cost` 1 | Workers |

A rule a store cannot enforce fails at startup with `MIU_E_RATELIMIT_UNSUPPORTED`.

`redisStore` accepts ioredis, Upstash, Bun's client (`incrby`, `pexpire`, `get`) or node-redis v4 (`incrBy`, `pExpire`, `get`); `del` is needed for `reset`.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu } from "miujs";
import { durableObjectStore, rateLimit } from "@miujs/ratelimit";

export { RateLimiterDurableObject } from "@miujs/ratelimit";

export default miu({
  name: "edge-limits",
  plugins: [
    rateLimit({
      store: durableObjectStore(),
      trustProxyHeader: "cf-connecting-ip",
      headers: "draft-8",
      rules: [{ match: { path: "/api/*", method: "POST" }, limit: 30, window: "1m", algorithm: "token-bucket", burst: 10 }],
    }),
  ],
});
```

### With @miujs/auth

```ts
auth({ rateLimit: { limiter: asAuthLimiter(durableObjectStore()) } });
```

`asAuthLimiter(store)` uses fixed windows, like auth's own limiter.

## Options

`rateLimit(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rules` | `RateLimitRule[]` | required | At least one rule. |
| `store` | `RateLimitStore` | `memoryStore()` | Where counters live. |
| `keyBy` | `By` | `"ip"` | Identity for rules without `by`. |
| `trustProxyHeader` | `string` | none (`ctx.ip`) | Proxy header holding the client IP; rightmost entry used. |
| `headers` | `"draft-6" \| "draft-8" \| false` | `"draft-6"` | `RateLimit-*` headers, or `RateLimit` + `RateLimit-Policy`, or none. |
| `onStoreError` | `"deny" \| "allow"` | `"deny"` | On store failure: 503, or log and allow. |
| `now` | `() => number` | `Date.now` | Clock, for tests. |

Rule fields:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `rule_<n>` | Counter and policy name. Letters, digits, `_ . -`. |
| `match` | `{ route?, path?, method?, tag? }` | every request | Which requests the rule counts. |
| `limit` | `number` | required | Requests (or cost units) per window. |
| `window` | `number \| string` | required | Seconds, or `"1m"` style. |
| `algorithm` | `"fixed" \| "sliding" \| "token-bucket"` | `"sliding"` | Counting algorithm. |
| `burst` | `number` | `limit` | Token bucket capacity. |
| `cost` | `number` | `1` | Units each request costs. |
| `by` | `By` | plugin `keyBy` | Who the rule counts. |

`limiter(options)` takes `limit`, `window`, `algorithm` (default `"sliding"`), `burst`, `store` (default `memoryStore()`), `name` (default `"limiter"`, the key prefix) and `now`.

Store options: `memoryStore` `maxKeys` (default `100000`); `kvStore` and `redisStore` `prefix` (default `"ratelimit:"`); `durableObjectStore` binding (default `"RATE_LIMITER"`); `cloudflareBindingStore` `limit`, `period` (10 or 60) and optional `namespaceId`.

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, `rateLimit()` shows a **Rate limits** section:

- **Status**: store, number of rules, keys tracked (memory store only; other stores say they cannot count), 429s and store errors in this instance since it started, and a table of rules with their rejections.
- **Settings**: `limit` and `window` per rule (e.g. `{ api: { limit: 200, window: "1m" } }`). They apply at once in this instance; the admin persists them and re-applies them on start. A value the store cannot enforce (e.g. a Cloudflare binding's fixed limit) is rejected and nothing changes. Lowering a limit can start affected clients on a fresh window.
- **Limited clients** list (memory store only; paged, search, filter limited/all). API keys appear only as their hash. Row action: reset.
- **Action** `resetKey`: forget one client (`ip:203.0.113.7`, `user:<id>`, `key:<hash>`) for a rule. Not available on `cloudflareBindingStore()`, which cannot reset.

Counters are per instance; `limiter()` instances are not part of the plugin and do not appear.

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_RATE_LIMITED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_rate_limited): 429, the request exceeded a rule; see `Retry-After`.
- [`MIU_E_RATELIMIT_CONFIG`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ratelimit_config): invalid rule, window, algorithm or option.
- [`MIU_E_RATELIMIT_UNSUPPORTED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ratelimit_unsupported): the store cannot enforce a rule, or cannot reset keys.
- [`MIU_E_RATELIMIT_ORDER`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ratelimit_order): a `by: "user"` rule but `auth()` is listed after `rateLimit()`.
- [`MIU_E_RATELIMIT_BINDING`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ratelimit_binding): KV, Durable Object or rate limiting binding missing.
- [`MIU_E_RATELIMIT_STORE`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ratelimit_store): 503, the store failed and `onStoreError` is `"deny"`.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

`memoryStore()` counts per isolate on Workers (the plugin logs a warning outside dev). Use one of the Workers stores; each reports its binding to `miu deploy cloudflare`.

`durableObjectStore()` (exact) needs the class exported from your Worker entry, as in the example above, and a binding:

```toml
[[durable_objects.bindings]]
name = "RATE_LIMITER"
class_name = "RateLimiterDurableObject"
```

`kvStore("RL_KV")` needs a KV namespace (`[[kv_namespaces]] binding = "RL_KV"`). It is approximate and allows about one write per second per key.

`cloudflareBindingStore("RL", { limit: 100, period: 60 })` uses Cloudflare's Rate Limiting binding. Every rule using it must have the same `limit` and `window`:

```toml
[[ratelimits]]
name = "RL"
namespace_id = "1001"
simple = { limit = 100, period = 60 }
```

`redisStore` works wherever your Redis client does (e.g. Upstash over HTTP on Workers).

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/AGENTS.md)

<!-- source: packages/bots/README.md -->

# @miujs/bots

> Bot, AI crawler and visitor-location detection for MiuJS, with a per-visitor policy that blocks, trims, or serves cached responses so crawlers never reach your handlers or database.

`@miujs/bots` adds `ctx.visitor` to every request: what kind of client it is (`human`, `search`, `ai`, `bot` or `unknown`), its name (`GPTBot`, `Googlebot`, `curl`), whether Cloudflare verified it, its bot score, and its country, region, city and network. A policy then decides what each visitor gets: `full` (the handler runs), `partial` (the handler runs and the JSON body is trimmed), `cached` (a stored response, the handler runs once per URL per hour), or `block`. Signals come from Cloudflare first (`request.cf` on Workers, trusted `cf-*` headers behind Cloudflare elsewhere), then the User-Agent, then the headers real browsers send.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/bots miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

With no options, humans get full access and every other visitor gets cached GET and HEAD responses: the first crawler request for a URL runs the handler, the rest are served from memory for an hour.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { bots } from "@miujs/bots";

let queries = 0;

export const getPost = route.get("/posts/:id", {
  params: t.object({ id: t.string() }),
  handler: ({ params, visitor }) => {
    queries++; // stands in for a database query
    return { id: params.id, title: "Hello", servedTo: visitor.kind };
  },
});

const app = miu({ name: "blog", routes: [getPost], plugins: [bots()] });
export default app;

const crawler = { headers: { "user-agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; GPTBot/1.2; +https://openai.com/gptbot)" } };
const first = await app.fetch(new Request("http://localhost/posts/1", crawler));
console.log(first.headers.get("x-miu-bot-cache")); // "miss": the handler ran
await first.text();
await app.drain(); // the copy is stored in the background
const second = await app.fetch(new Request("http://localhost/posts/1?utm_source=feed", crawler));
console.log(second.headers.get("x-miu-bot-cache"), queries); // "hit" 1
```

Responses carry `x-miu-bot-cache: miss | hit | stale` when the bot cache was used.

## Visitors

`ctx.visitor` is set on every request, before validation and auth checks:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"human"`, `"search"` (verified search engine), `"ai"`, `"bot"` or `"unknown"`. |
| `name` | The agent, e.g. `"GPTBot"`, `"ClaudeBot"`, `"Googlebot"`, `"curl"`, `"AhrefsBot"`. |
| `verified` | Cloudflare (`verifiedBot`) or your `verify` hook confirmed the claim. |
| `score` | Cloudflare bot score, 1–99 (lower is more bot-like). Needs Bot Management. |
| `country`, `region`, `city`, `continent`, `asn`, `asOrg` | Location from Cloudflare. `country` is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`T1` is Tor). |
| `access` | What this request gets: `"full"`, `"partial"`, `"cached"` or `"block"`. |

How the kind is decided, strongest signal first:

1. A User-Agent naming an AI agent or automation tool (`GPTBot`, `ClaudeBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Bytespider`, `curl`, `python-requests`, `HeadlessChrome`, any `...bot`/`crawler`/`spider`/`scraper`) is `ai` or `bot`. A good score never upgrades a client that says it is a bot.
2. A User-Agent claiming a search engine (`Googlebot`, `Bingbot`, `DuckDuckBot`, `Applebot`, `YandexBot`, `Baiduspider`) is `search` only when verified, else `bot`. Anyone can send `Googlebot` in a header.
3. Cloudflare verified bots get their kind from `verifiedBotCategory` (AI categories are `ai`, "Search Engine Crawler" is `search`, others `bot`). A bot score below `botScoreThreshold` (default 30) is `bot`.
4. A browser User-Agent is `human` when Cloudflare scored it (30 or more) or passed JavaScript detection; otherwise it must send `accept-language`, and Chromium 80+ and Firefox 90+ must also send `sec-fetch-mode` on secure origins (https, `x-forwarded-proto: https`, or localhost; Chrome omits `sec-fetch-*` on plain http). Safari is not required to send them. A browser User-Agent failing these is `unknown`.
5. No User-Agent, or one that is neither a browser nor a known agent, is `unknown`.

The header checks only catch careless clients: a crawler that copies every browser header looks human. For real detection, put the site behind Cloudflare and turn on Bot Fight Mode (free) or Bot Management (bot scores), plus AI Crawl Control to see and block AI crawlers at the edge.

The agent list is exported as `AGENTS` (`AI_AGENTS`, `SEARCH_AGENTS`, `AUTOMATION_AGENTS`) and replaceable with `bots({ agents })`. `classifyUserAgent(ua)` and `detectVisitor(request, { runtime })` work outside the plugin. Classification is one precompiled regex over the list (plus one for generic automation words) and is memoized per User-Agent string in a bounded LRU.

## Blocking AI crawlers

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { bots } from "@miujs/bots";

const app = miu({
  routes: [route.get("/articles", { handler: () => ({ articles: [] }) })],
  plugins: [
    bots({
      policy: { ai: "block" },
      robots: { disallowAI: true, disallow: ["/admin"], sitemap: "https://example.com/sitemap.xml" },
      xRobotsTag: "noai, noimageai",
    }),
  ],
});

const res = await app.fetch(new Request("http://localhost/articles", { headers: { "user-agent": "ClaudeBot/1.0" } }));
console.log(res.status); // 403, error code MIU_E_BOT_BLOCKED
```

Blocked requests get `MIU_E_BOT_BLOCKED` with status `blockStatus` (403 by default; 404, 410, 429 with `Retry-After`, or 451) and a debug log line. `robots` serves `GET /robots.txt`: one group disallowing `/` for every AI agent in the list plus the robots-only opt-out tokens (`Google-Extended`, `Applebot-Extended`, ...), then your rules for everyone else. robots.txt is a request; `block` is enforcement.

## Partial data for bots

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { bots, pickFields } from "@miujs/bots";

export const listProducts = route.get("/products", {
  name: "listProducts",
  handler: ({ visitor }) => {
    // Read access yourself to skip expensive work...
    const withStock = visitor.access === "full";
    return { items: [{ id: 1, name: "Lamp", price: 30, stock: withStock ? 4 : undefined }] };
  },
});

export const getProduct = route.get("/products/:id", {
  handler: ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id, name: "Lamp", price: 30, supplier: "ACME", margin: 0.4 }),
});

miu({
  routes: [listProducts, getProduct],
  plugins: [
    bots({
      policy: { search: "partial", bot: "partial", unknown: "partial" },
      routes: [
        // ...or let the plugin trim the JSON body: a list of top-level fields, or a function.
        { match: { route: "listProducts" }, partial: (data: any) => ({ items: pickFields(data.items, ["id", "name"]) }) },
        { match: { path: "/products/:id" }, partial: ["id", "name", "price"] },
      ],
    }),
  ],
});
```

Partial GET responses are cached too, under a key separate from `cached` ones.

### Per-route settings

Set them on the route with the typed `bots` option (`false` exempts the route), or from the plugin with `routes` entries:

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { bots } from "@miujs/bots";

export const members = route.get("/members", {
  bots: { policy: { ai: "block", bot: "block" } },
  handler: () => ({ members: [] }),
});
export const status = route.get("/status", { bots: false, handler: () => ({ up: true }) });
export const card = route.get("/cards/:id", {
  bots: { policy: { bot: "partial" }, partial: ["id", "title"], ttl: 600 },
  handler: ({ params }) => ({ id: params.id, title: "Card", body: "..." }),
});

miu({ routes: [members, status, card], plugins: [bots({ routes: [{ match: { path: "/admin/*" }, policy: { ai: "block" } }] })] });
```

The route option takes `policy`, `exempt`, `partial` and `ttl`, and wins over any matching `routes` entry. An invalid one fails that route's requests with `MIU_E_BOTS_CONFIG`. Route rules match like `@miujs/ratelimit` rules (`route`, `path`, `method`, `tag`; `/blog/*` is the path and everything below); the first match applies. A route rule can also set `policy` (e.g. `{ ai: "block" }` on one route), `exempt: true` (full access for everyone) and `ttl`.

## Per-country rules

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route } from "miujs";
import { bots } from "@miujs/bots";

export const home = route.get("/", {
  handler: ({ visitor }) => ({ greeting: visitor.country === "VN" ? "Xin chào" : "Hello", city: visitor.city ?? null }),
});

export default miu({
  routes: [home],
  plugins: [
    bots({
      trustCloudflare: true, // Bun/Node behind Cloudflare only; Workers read request.cf automatically
      blockCountries: ["KP"],
      rules: [
        { when: (v) => v.verified, action: "cached" }, // verified crawlers are never country-blocked
        { when: (v) => v.kind === "ai" && v.country === "CN", action: "block" },
      ],
      cache: { varyByCountry: true },
    }),
  ],
});
```

The decision order is: always-exempt routes (`/_miu/*`, the MCP endpoint, `/robots.txt`), a route rule with `exempt`, `rules` in order, `blockCountries`, `allowCountries` (visitors with no known country are not blocked), signed-in users (full), the route rule's `policy`, then `policy`.

## Signed-in users and what is never cached

List `auth()` before `bots()` (startup fails with `MIU_E_BOTS_ORDER` otherwise). A request with `ctx.user` bypasses kind-based caching, partial trimming and blocking, whatever its User-Agent; `rules` and country lists still apply. The bot cache only serves and stores:

- GET (HEAD is answered from the GET entry, never stored) on a matched route, without `Authorization` or `Upgrade` headers;
- responses with a status in `cache.statuses` (default 200), no `Set-Cookie` (including `ctx.cookies.set`), no `Cache-Control: private | no-store | no-cache`, no `Vary` other than `Accept-Encoding`, not `text/event-stream`, at most `maxEntryBytes`.

The key is `GET` + access level + host + path + sorted query without tracking parameters (`TRACKING_PARAMS`: `utm_*`, `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, `ref`, ...), plus the country with `varyByCountry` and your `varyBy(ctx)`. Concurrent misses for one key run the handler once; the others wait for its response, for up to `cache.waitMs` (default 10000 ms). After that they run the handler themselves rather than hang behind a stuck request; the first request still finishes and stores its response. With `staleWhileRevalidate`, an expired copy is served (`x-miu-bot-cache: stale`) while one background request refreshes it.

## Budgets

Cap how often each kind may reach your handlers with a `limiter()` from `@miujs/ratelimit`. Cache hits are free; requests are counted per agent name (all GPTBot traffic shares one budget), else per IP.

```ts
import { limiter } from "@miujs/ratelimit";
bots({ budget: { ai: limiter({ limit: 60, window: "1m", name: "ai" }), unknown: limiter({ limit: 600, window: "1m", name: "unknown" }) } });
```

Over budget: 429 `MIU_E_RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`.

## Stores

| Store | Shared by | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `memoryBotStore({ maxEntries, maxBytes })` | one process / isolate | Default. LRU, 1000 entries and 32 MiB by default. |
| `cacheClientStore()` | everything on the same backend | Uses `ctx.cache` from `@miujs/cache` (KV on Workers, Redis, memory). List `cache()` first. Long keys are hashed. |
| `cacheApiStore()` | one Cloudflare data center | Workers Cache API (`caches.default`), no binding needed. |

On Workers without `cache.store`, the plugin uses `ctx.cache` when `@miujs/cache` is listed first, else the Cache API, else memory. A store is `{ name, get(key, ctx), set(key, entry, ctx), delete?, size?, bytes?, purge?, inspect?, cloudflare? }`.

## Options

`bots(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy` | `{ [kind]: Access }` | human `full`, others `cached` | Action per visitor kind. |
| `rules` | `{ when(visitor, ctx), action }[]` | `[]` | Checked first; first match decides. |
| `blockCountries` | `string[]` | none | Countries that are blocked. |
| `allowCountries` | `string[]` | none | Only these countries (unknown country passes). |
| `routes` | `BotRouteRule[]` | `[]` | Per-route `policy`, `exempt`, `partial`, `ttl` by `match`; the route's own `bots` option wins. |
| `partial` | `string[] \| (data, ctx) => unknown` | none | Default trimming for partial visitors. |
| `agents` | `AgentEntry[]` | `AGENTS` | Known agents: `{ token, kind, name? }`. |
| `trustCloudflare` | `boolean` | `false` | Read `cf-*` headers off Workers. Only when all traffic comes through Cloudflare. |
| `botScoreThreshold` | `number` | `30` | Cloudflare scores below it are bots. |
| `strictHeaders` | `boolean` | `false` | Require `sec-fetch-*` on plain http too. |
| `verify` | `(req, { kind, name }) => boolean` | none | Confirm a search/AI claim Cloudflare did not (e.g. reverse DNS). |
| `blockStatus` | `403 \| 404 \| 410 \| 429 \| 451` | `403` | Status of blocked responses. |
| `cache` | `BotsCacheOptions \| false` | memory | `store`, `ttl` (3600 s), `staleWhileRevalidate` (0), `statuses` ([200]), `maxEntryBytes` (1 MiB), `waitMs` (10000), `varyByCountry`, `ignoreParams`, `varyBy`. `false`: cached visitors reach handlers. |
| `robots` | `boolean \| RobotsOptions` | off | Serve `/robots.txt`: `disallowAI` (true), `disallow`, `allow`, `sitemap`, `extra`. |
| `xRobotsTag` | `string \| (visitor) => string` | none | `X-Robots-Tag` on responses without one. |
| `budget` | `{ [kind]: limiter }` | none | Rate limits on handler-reaching requests. |
| `now` | `() => number` | `Date.now` | Clock, for tests. |
| `timers` | `{ set(fn, ms), clear(handle) }` | `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` | Timers for `waitMs`, for tests. |

`miu inspect` shows the policy, cache settings and counters by kind, by action and for the cache (hit, stale, miss, coalesced, stored, skipped, waitTimeouts).

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, `bots()` shows a **Bots** section:

- **Status**: requests by kind and by decision, blocked and over-budget counts, and the bot cache: store, entries and size (memory store; other stores say they cannot count), hits, misses, hit rate, stale served, stored, not stored, errors and wait timeouts. Counters are per instance since it started.
- **Settings**: `policy` per kind, `blockCountries`, `allowCountries` (empty = no restriction), `botScoreThreshold` (1–99) and `cacheTtl` (when the cache is on). They apply at once in this instance; the admin persists them and re-applies them on start.
- **Recently blocked** list: the last 200 blocked visits in this instance (time, kind, agent, country, path without the query string, and the reason: policy, route policy, rule n, country blocked, country not allowed). Filter by kind; search agent, country or path.
- **Actions**: `purgeCache` (danger; all or under a path prefix, memory store only), `purgeUrl` (one page on any store with `delete`; on KV or the Cache API, entries varied by country or `varyBy` cannot be found), and `classifyUserAgent` (what a User-Agent claims and the access its kind gets; nothing is verified without Cloudflare or `verify`).

## Errors

- [`MIU_E_BOT_BLOCKED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_bot_blocked): the policy blocked this visitor (status `blockStatus`).
- [`MIU_E_BOTS_CONFIG`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_bots_config): an invalid option, or a store used where it cannot work.
- [`MIU_E_BOTS_ORDER`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_bots_order): `auth()` is listed after `bots()`.
- [`MIU_E_RATE_LIMITED`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_rate_limited): a `budget` limiter is exhausted.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

On Workers, `request.cf` gives location, ASN and (with Bot Management) `botManagement.score`, `verifiedBot`, `verifiedBotCategory` and `jsDetection.passed`; nothing needs configuring. Turn on Bot Fight Mode or Bot Management and AI Crawl Control in the dashboard so most bad traffic never reaches the Worker, and use this plugin for what gets through. Each isolate has its own memory store: use `cacheClientStore()` with a KV-backed `cache()` (binding `CACHE`) or `cacheApiStore()` to share cached responses. On Bun, Deno or Node behind Cloudflare (proxy or Tunnel), enable the "Add visitor location headers" and "Add bot protection headers" managed transforms and set `trustCloudflare: true`; never set it when clients can reach the origin directly.

## Links

- [Getting started guide](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/guide.md)
- [Error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md)
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/AGENTS.md)
