<!-- source: packages/workflows/README.md -->

# @miujs/workflows

> Durable workflows for MiuJS: event, cron, webhook and manual triggers, journaled steps, sleeps, waits for events and approvals, JSON-defined workflows, routes and MCP tools.

`@miujs/workflows` runs automation that survives restarts and deploys while it sleeps or waits. A workflow's `run` function is replayed from the top on every resume; each `step.*` call is journaled, so completed steps return their recorded result instead of running again. Runs are resumed through `@miujs/queue` and stored in memory or in a SQL database through `@miujs/db`. Use it for follow-ups, approvals, onboarding sequences and other multi-day processes, and when agents should be able to start and inspect runs.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/workflows miujs @miujs/db @miujs/queue
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, t } from "miujs";
import { defineWorkflow, workflows } from "@miujs/workflows";

export const hello = defineWorkflow("hello", {
  input: t.object({ name: t.string() }),
  run: async ({ input, step }) => {
    const greeting = await step.run("greet", async () => `hi ${input.name}`);
    return { greeting };
  },
});

const wf = workflows({ workflows: [hello] }); // memory run store and queue by default
const app = miu({ name: "automation", plugins: [wf], mcp: true });
await app.ready();

const { id } = await wf.start("hello", { name: "Ann" });
console.log(id, (await wf.getRun(id)).status);

export default app;
```

The plugin object also has `emit(event, data)`, `listRuns(filter)`, `cancel(id)`, `retry(id)` (resume a failed run from its failed step) and `decide(runId, step, user, decision, comment)`. In requests, `ctx.events.emit(event, data, { idempotencyKey })` starts event-triggered workflows and resumes runs waiting for that event.

## Steps

Code outside `step.*` calls must be deterministic: do side effects in `step.run`, and use `step.now()` / `step.uuid()` instead of `Date.now()` / `crypto.randomUUID()`. Step names must be unique within a run.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { t } from "miujs";
import { NonRetryableError, defineWorkflow, on } from "@miujs/workflows";

async function enrich(email: string) {
  if (!email.includes("@")) throw new NonRetryableError("not an email"); // fail now, no retries
  return { email, company: email.split("@")[1] };
}

export const followUp = defineWorkflow("contact-follow-up", {
  trigger: on("contact.created"),
  input: t.object({ contactId: t.string(), email: t.string() }),
  concurrency: { key: (input) => input.contactId, limit: 1 },
  run: async ({ input, step, log }) => {
    const lead = await step.run("enrich", () => enrich(input.email), { retries: 5, backoff: "exponential" });
    await step.sleep("wait-a-day", "1d");
    const reply = await step.waitForEvent("reply", { event: "email.replied", match: { "data.contactId": input.contactId }, timeout: "3d" });
    if (!reply) {
      const decision = await step.waitForApproval("send-follow-up", { approvers: { role: "manager" }, timeout: "2d" });
      if (decision?.decision === "approve") await step.run("follow-up", () => log.info("following up", { company: lead.company }));
    }
  },
});
```

| Step | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `step.run(name, fn, { retries, backoff })` | Run once; the JSON result is journaled. Retried on throw (default 3 retries, exponential backoff). |
| `step.sleep(name, duration)` / `step.sleepUntil(name, time)` | Pause durably. Durations: `"1d"`, `"12h"`, `"3 days"` or milliseconds. |
| `step.waitForEvent(name, { event, match, timeout })` | Park until a matching event; `null` on timeout. |
| `step.waitForApproval(name, { approvers, timeout })` | Park until an approver decides via `POST /workflows/approvals/:runId/:step`; `null` on timeout. |
| `step.now(name?)` / `step.uuid(name?)` | Journaled time and UUID. |

A step that fails every attempt throws `StepFailedError` into the workflow code.

## Triggers

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { cron, defineWorkflow, manual, on, webhook } from "@miujs/workflows";

export const weekly = defineWorkflow("weekly-report", {
  trigger: [
    cron("0 9 * * 1"),                                                      // 5-field UTC cron
    on("deal.updated", { match: { "data.stage": "won" } }),                 // event with a match
    webhook("/hooks/form", { secret: (env) => env.FORM_SECRET as string }), // POST, HMAC-SHA256 in x-signature
    manual(),                                                               // code, API or MCP only
  ],
  run: async ({ run }) => ({ trigger: run.trigger.type }),
});
```

Without `trigger`, a workflow is manual. Every workflow can also be started manually.

## JSON workflows

`fromJson` turns a JSON spec (the format a visual builder saves) into a workflow that runs on the same engine. `validateSpec` returns precise issues with a `path`, `message` and `fix`. Built-in actions are `http`, `send_email` and `log`; add your own with `defineAction`. Strings support `{{ expression }}` templates over `data`, `input` and `steps`.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { t } from "miujs";
import { defineAction, fromJson, validateSpec, workflows } from "@miujs/workflows";

const updateRecord = defineAction("update_record", {
  description: "Update a CRM record",
  params: t.object({ id: t.string(), fields: t.record(t.unknown()) }),
  run: async (params) => ({ updated: params.id }),
});

const spec = {
  name: "deal-flow",
  trigger: { type: "event", event: "deal.updated" },
  steps: [
    {
      id: "check",
      type: "condition",
      if: "data.amount > 10000 && data.stage == 'won'",
      then: [{ id: "approve", type: "approval", approvers: { role: "manager" }, timeout: "2d" }],
      else: [{ id: "small", type: "action", action: "log", params: { message: "small deal {{ data.id }}" } }],
    },
    { id: "record", type: "action", action: "update_record", params: { id: "{{ data.id }}", fields: { amount: "{{ data.amount }}" } } },
  ],
};

const checked = validateSpec(spec, { actions: [updateRecord] });
if (!checked.ok) console.log(checked.issues);

export const dealFlow = fromJson(spec, { actions: [updateRecord] });
export const plugin = workflows({ workflows: [dealFlow] });
```

Step types: `action`, `condition`, `wait`, `wait_for_event`, `approval`. Trigger types: `event`, `cron`, `webhook` (with `secretEnv`, `header`), `manual`.

## Routes and MCP

Routes (all `auth: "required"`, under `prefix`, default `/workflows`):

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /workflows` | List workflows, triggers and input schemas. |
| `POST /workflows/:name/runs` | Start a run: body `{ input }`. |
| `GET /workflows/runs`, `GET /workflows/runs/:id` | List runs; one run with its step timeline. |
| `POST /workflows/runs/:id/cancel`, `POST /workflows/runs/:id/retry` | Cancel; retry from the failed step. |
| `POST /workflows/events` | Emit an event: body `{ event, data, idempotencyKey }`. |
| `POST /workflows/approvals/:runId/:step` | Decide: body `{ decision: "approve" \| "reject", comment }`. |

With `miu({ mcp: true })`, agents get the tools `workflows_list`, `workflow_start`, `workflow_runs`, `workflow_run` and `emit_event`. Routes and tools check `ctx.authorize(permission)` when it exists, with the permissions `workflows:read`, `workflows:run`, `workflows:manage` and `workflows:emit` (rename them with `permissions`).

## Durable storage

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { sqlite } from "@miujs/db";
import { defineWorkflow, dbRunStore, workflows } from "@miujs/workflows";

const ping = defineWorkflow("ping", { run: async ({ step }) => step.now("at") });

export const plugin = workflows({
  workflows: [ping],
  store: dbRunStore(sqlite("app.db")), // tables are created on first use (workflowMigrations)
  mailer: { send: async (msg) => console.log("send_email", msg) }, // any object with send(msg)
});
```

`memoryRunStore()` (the default) loses runs on restart. Use `dbRunStore(sqlite(path))` on a server or `dbRunStore(d1("DB"))` on Workers.

The memory store is bounded so a long-running process does not grow: it keeps the newest 1000 finished (completed, failed, cancelled) runs with their step journals, and remembers event idempotency keys for 24 hours, up to 10 000 keys. Active runs are always kept. To change the limits, pass `memoryRunStore({ maxFinishedRuns: 5000, idempotencyTtlMs: 3_600_000, maxIdempotencyKeys: 50_000 })`. A finished run that has been dropped can no longer be read or retried.

## Options

`workflows(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `workflows` | `WorkflowDef[]` | required | Workflows from `defineWorkflow()` or `fromJson()`. |
| `store` | `RunStore` | `memoryRunStore()` | Run storage; `dbRunStore(database)` survives restarts. |
| `adapter` | `QueueAdapter` | `memoryQueue()`; on Workers `cloudflareQueue({ binding: "WORKFLOWS_QUEUE", queue: "miu-workflows" })` | Queue that resumes runs. |
| `clock` | `Clock` | `realClock` | Time source (`manualClock()` in tests). |
| `maxDelaySeconds` | `number` | 12 h on Cloudflare, unlimited otherwise | Longest single queue delay; longer sleeps are chained. |
| `leaseMs` | `number` | `900000` (15 min) | How long one invocation may hold a run. |
| `env` | `Env` | process env | Env for work started outside a request. |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | `globalThis.fetch` | fetch for steps and the `http` action. |
| `mailer` | `{ send(msg) }` | a plugin named `mail` with `send()`, if any | Mailer for the `send_email` action. |
| `prefix` | `string` | `"/workflows"` | Route prefix. |
| `permissions` | `Partial<{ read, run, manage, emit }>` | `workflows:read`, `workflows:run`, `workflows:manage`, `workflows:emit` | Permission names checked with `ctx.authorize`. |

`defineWorkflow(name, config)`: `run` (required), `input` (a `t` schema; default any object), `trigger` (one or an array; default `manual()`), `description`, `concurrency: { key(input), limit }` (limit default `1`).

## Admin (`manage()`)

With `@miujs/admin`, the plugin shows a **Workflows** section next to the admin's workflow builder (which edits definitions; this section operates runs):

- **Status**: registered and disabled workflows, runs queued, running, sleeping, waiting and failed (each counted up to 200, then shown as `200+`), the store and queue in use, a **Workflows** table (triggers, enabled) and the 5 most recent failures.
- **Runs** list, newest first, filtered by workflow and status; search finds a run by id. Rows never include the resume token, and inputs hide secret-looking keys. Row actions: `cancel` (danger), `retry` (failed runs, from the failed step) and `wakeNow` (sleeping or waiting runs, see below). They answer with a message instead of failing when there is nothing to do.
- **Actions**: `start` (start a workflow with JSON input as a manual run by the operator) and `emit` (send an event with optional data and idempotency key).
- **Settings**: `disabled`, a list of workflow names that start no new runs from any trigger (event, cron, webhook, manual, admin). Runs already started go on; cancel them from the runs list. Starting a disabled workflow fails with `MIU_E_CONFLICT` (409); emit reports it under `skipped`; cron firings are skipped without retries.

`wakeNow` (not marked dangerous) wakes a run now instead of at its timer:

- In `step.sleep` / `step.sleepUntil`: the sleep ends now and the run continues with the next step.
- In `step.waitForEvent`: the wait times out now, so the step returns `null` exactly as on its `timeout` (also for waits without one). An event that arrives before the run resumes still wins.
- In `step.waitForApproval`: refused with `MIU_E_CONFLICT` (409); approve or reject it instead.

It works the same on every run store: the step's journaled wake-up time moves to now and the run gets a new resume token, so the original timer message does nothing when it fires. Waking twice wakes once; a run that is no longer sleeping or waiting is left alone ("nothing to do").

## Errors

- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_CONFIG`: invalid `defineWorkflow`, trigger, action or plugin options.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_DUPLICATE`: two workflows share a name.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN`: no workflow with this name.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_RUN_NOT_FOUND` / `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_RUN_STATE`: unknown run, or the run cannot be cancelled or retried in its current state.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_STEP_DUPLICATE`: two steps in one run share a name.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_DURATION`: a duration such as `"1d"` could not be parsed.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_SPEC_INVALID` / `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_ACTION_UNKNOWN` / `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_EXPRESSION`: problems in a JSON spec.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_SIGNATURE`: a webhook signature did not match.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_NOT_APPROVER` / `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING`: the user may not decide, or nothing is waiting for approval.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_EVENT_RESERVED`: `workflow.approval` cannot be emitted; use the approvals route.
- `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_MAILER_MISSING`: `send_email` ran without a mailer.

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md), e.g. [`MIU_E_WORKFLOW_CONFIG`](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_workflow_config).

## Cloudflare Workers

The default engine resumes runs through Cloudflare Queues (binding `WORKFLOWS_QUEUE`); cron triggers become Worker cron triggers. Store runs in D1 with `dbRunStore(d1("DB"))`. `miu deploy cloudflare` declares the queue (named after the app, here `crm`) and crons:

```toml
[[queues.producers]]
binding = "WORKFLOWS_QUEUE"
queue = "crm-workflows-queue"

[[queues.consumers]]
queue = "crm-workflows-queue"

[triggers]
crons = ["0 9 * * 1"]
```

Add a `[[d1_databases]]` binding named `DB` yourself if you use `d1("DB")`. Queue delays are capped at 12 hours on Cloudflare; longer sleeps are chained automatically.

Alternatively, run a code-defined workflow on Cloudflare Workflows with `createCloudflareWorkflow(def)`. workerd only runs Workflow classes that extend `WorkflowEntrypoint` from `cloudflare:workers`, so on Workers the class extends it: `@miujs/workflows` loads that module itself (elsewhere, such as Bun in tests, it uses a stand-in with the same shape). Pass `{ base: WorkflowEntrypoint }` to choose the base class yourself. If the module cannot be loaded on Workers, `createCloudflareWorkflow` throws `MIU_E_WORKFLOW_CONFIG` with that fix, instead of workerd failing later with "worker is not an actor". `miu deploy cloudflare` can load an entry that imports `cloudflare:workers`. `step.run` maps to `step.do`, sleeps and `waitForEvent` map directly, and `waitForApproval` waits for an event of type `approval-<step>`.

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { createCloudflareWorkflow, defineWorkflow } from "@miujs/workflows";

const nightly = defineWorkflow("nightly", { run: async ({ step }) => step.run("tick", () => 1) });

// wrangler: [[workflows]] name = "nightly" binding = "NIGHTLY" class_name = "Nightly"
export const Nightly = createCloudflareWorkflow(nightly);
```

`sqlite()` from `@miujs/db` runs on Bun only; the memory store and memory queue work everywhere.

<!-- source: packages/ai/README.md -->

# @miujs/ai

> Model calls for MiuJS: `ctx.ai` for generate, stream, typed objects, embeddings, a tool-use agent loop and RAG, over Anthropic, OpenAI-compatible APIs, Workers AI and Cloudflare AI Gateway.

`@miujs/ai` adds `ctx.ai` to every request through the `ai()` plugin, and `createAI()` gives the same client to jobs, workflows and scripts. Providers are plain `fetch` (or the Workers AI binding), so it runs on every MiuJS runtime. `appTools(app)` hands the app's own routes to the model as tools, with the caller's auth applied. Use it when routes need an LLM: chat endpoints, extraction into `t` schemas, agents, or question answering over your documents.

## Install

```bash
bun add @miujs/ai miujs
```

Bun runs the TypeScript source; Node and Deno get prebuilt JS with `.d.ts` types (npm packages are not published yet).

## Quick start

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { ai, anthropic } from "@miujs/ai";

export const summarize = route.post("/summarize", {
  body: t.object({ text: t.string() }),
  handler: async ({ ai, body }) => {
    const out = await ai.generate({ system: "Summarize in one sentence.", prompt: body.text });
    return { summary: out.text, usage: out.usage };
  },
});

// Reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the request env (process env locally, secrets on Workers).
export default miu({ routes: [summarize], plugins: [ai({ provider: anthropic() })] });
```

`generate()` returns `{ text, toolCalls, usage, stopReason, model, message }`. Append `message` to `messages` for a follow-up turn.

## Typed output

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { t } from "miujs";
import { anthropic, createAI } from "@miujs/ai";

const client = createAI({ provider: anthropic(), env: { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: "sk-ant-..." } });

const Person = t.object({ name: t.string({ minLength: 2 }), age: t.integer({ min: 0 }), tags: t.optional(t.array(t.string())) });
const person = await client.object({ schema: Person, prompt: "Ada Lovelace, 36" });
console.log(person.name, person.age); // typed as Infer<typeof Person>
```

`object()` uses the provider's structured-output mode, validates the reply with the schema, and retries once with the validation issues. A second failure throws `MIU_E_AI_INVALID_OUTPUT`.

## Streaming

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { route, t } from "miujs";
import { toSSE } from "@miujs/ai";

export const chat = route.post("/chat", {
  body: t.object({ q: t.string() }),
  handler: ({ ai, body }) => toSSE(ai.stream({ prompt: body.q })),
});
```

`stream()` yields `{ type: "text" }`, `{ type: "tool_call" }` and a final `{ type: "finish", stopReason, usage, model, message }`. `toSSE()` sends each as a server-sent event named after its type, and an `error` event with the MiuError JSON if the stream fails.

## Tools and agents

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { miu, route, t } from "miujs";
import { ai, anthropic, appTools, tool } from "@miujs/ai";

const add = tool({
  name: "add",
  description: "Add two numbers",
  input: t.object({ a: t.number(), b: t.number() }),
  run: ({ a, b }) => ({ sum: a + b }),
});

export const listNotes = route.get("/notes", { summary: "List notes", handler: () => [{ id: "n1", text: "hi" }] });

export const agent = route.post("/agent", {
  body: t.object({ prompt: t.string() }),
  handler: async ({ ai, body }) => {
    const out = await ai.run({
      prompt: body.prompt,
      tools: [add, appTools({ include: ["listNotes"] })],
      maxSteps: 5,
      limits: { totalTokens: 50_000, timeMs: 30_000 },
    });
    return { text: out.text, stopReason: out.stopReason, calls: out.toolCalls.map((c) => c.name) };
  },
});

export default miu({ routes: [listNotes, agent], plugins: [ai({ provider: anthropic() })] });
```

`run()` calls the model, runs the tools it asks for (in parallel), feeds the results back, and stops when the model answers or a limit is hit (`stopReason` is then `max_steps`, `token_limit` or `time_limit`). Tool arguments are validated against `input`; errors, including thrown `ToolError`s and `MiuError`s, go back to the model as error results instead of failing the run. `appTools()` uses `app.tools()`: the same tools MCP serves, dispatched through the app with the current request's `authorization`, `cookie` and `x-request-id` headers. Outside a request, pass the app and headers: `appTools(app, { headers: { authorization } })`.

## Embeddings and RAG

<!-- test -->
```ts
import { anthropic, createAI, memoryVectors, openaiCompatible } from "@miujs/ai";

const client = createAI({
  provider: anthropic(),
  embeddings: { provider: openaiCompatible({ baseUrl: "https://api.openai.com/v1", apiKeyEnv: "OPENAI_API_KEY" }), model: "text-embedding-3-small" },
});

const store = memoryVectors();
await client.index({ store, docs: [{ id: "cats", text: "Cats sleep 16 hours a day.", metadata: { source: "cats.md" } }] });

const { answer, sources } = await client.rag({ query: "How much do cats sleep?", store, topK: 1 });
console.log(answer, sources.map((s) => s.id));
```

Vector stores: `memoryVectors()` (in-process), `sqliteVectors(db, { table })` (float32 blobs in SQLite/D1, default table `miu_vectors`, brute-force cosine for small sets), `vectorize(binding, { indexName })` (Cloudflare Vectorize). `rag()` answers with `RAG_SYSTEM` unless you pass `system`, and cites sources as `[n]`.

## Providers

- `anthropic({ apiKey, apiKeyEnv, baseUrl, fallbacks, headers })`: Claude Messages API. Default model `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` (`claude-opus-5-5`). Supports prompt caching (`cache: true | "5m" | "1h"`). No embeddings.
- `openaiCompatible({ baseUrl, apiKey, apiKeyEnv, model, embedModel, structured, name, gatewaySlug, headers })`: any `/chat/completions` API (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio). Has embeddings.
- `workersAI(binding = "AI", { model, embedModel })`: Workers AI through `env.AI`. Defaults `WORKERS_AI_DEFAULT_MODEL` and `WORKERS_AI_DEFAULT_EMBED_MODEL`.
- `aiGateway({ accountId, gatewayId, token }, provider)`: routes one of the above through Cloudflare AI Gateway.

## Options

`ai(options)` and `createAI(options)`:

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provider` | `Provider` | required | `anthropic()`, `openaiCompatible()`, `workersAI()` or `aiGateway(...)`. |
| `model` | `string` | the provider's default | Default model for every call. |
| `embeddings` | `{ provider?, model? }` | the main provider | Separate provider/model for `embed()`, `index()` and `rag()`. |
| `maxTokens` | `number` | `16000` (`64000` for `stream`) | Default `max_tokens`. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | `120000` | Request timeout (for streams: until headers arrive). |
| `retries` | `number` | `2` | Retries on 429, 5xx and network errors, honoring `retry-after`. |
| `temperature` | `number` | the provider's | Default sampling temperature when a call passes none. |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch` | global `fetch` | Injected fetch (tests, proxies). |
| `env` | `Env` | process env | `createAI` only: where API keys and bindings are read. |
| `log` | `Logger` | a `createLogger("info")` | `createAI` only: usage is logged at debug level. |
| `stores` | `VectorStore[]` | `[]` | `ai()` only: stores whose bindings `miu deploy cloudflare` should declare. |

Per-call options for `generate` / `stream` / `object`: `system`, `prompt`, `messages`, `model`, `maxTokens`, `temperature`, `tools`, `cache`, `signal`, `extra`. `run` adds `tools` (required), `maxSteps` (default 10) and `limits: { totalTokens, timeMs }`. `rag` takes `query`, `store`, `topK` (default 4) and `filter`.

## Admin

`ai()` implements `manage()`, so `@miujs/admin` shows an **AI** section:

- **Status**: provider, model and embeddings names; completed requests, input/output tokens, tool calls, embedding calls, errors and the last error code, plus a per-model table (20 models, the rest under `(other)`). Counters are in memory, per process (per isolate on Workers). Keys, prompts, replies and provider error messages are never kept.
- **Settings**: default `model` (`null` = configured default), `maxTokens` and `temperature` (`null` = provider default), applied to later requests without a deploy.
- **Action** `testPrompt` (`{ prompt, maxTokens? }`, default 256 tokens): sends a prompt with the current settings and returns the reply (2000 characters at most), model, usage and stop reason. At most 5 per minute per process (`MIU_E_AI_TEST_RATE_LIMITED`).

## Errors

- `MIU_E_AI_MISSING_KEY`: the provider's API key env var is not set ([docs](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md#miu_e_ai_missing_key)).
- `MIU_E_AI_AUTH`: the provider rejected the key.
- `MIU_E_AI_RATE_LIMITED`: still rate limited after retries.
- `MIU_E_AI_BAD_REQUEST`: the provider rejected the request (model id, options).
- `MIU_E_AI_PROVIDER_ERROR`: the provider failed (5xx, network) after retries.
- `MIU_E_AI_TIMEOUT`: no answer within `timeoutMs`.
- `MIU_E_AI_INVALID_OUTPUT`: `object()` could not get JSON matching the schema.
- `MIU_E_AI_REFUSED`: the model declined the request.
- `MIU_E_AI_UNSUPPORTED`: the provider lacks a feature (for example embeddings on `anthropic()`).
- `MIU_E_AI_BINDING`: a Workers AI or Vectorize binding is missing from `env`.
- `MIU_E_AI_CONFIG`: invalid options (no model, no input, bad tool name).

See [all error codes](https://github.com/khangkhangg/miujs/blob/miujs-monorepo/docs/errors.md).

## Cloudflare Workers

Keys are read from the request `env` per call, so set them with `wrangler secret put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. `workersAI()` uses the `AI` binding by default and declares `[ai] binding = "AI"` through the plugin's `cloudflare()` (also when it is only the embeddings provider). `vectorize("DOCS", { indexName: "docs" })` listed in `ai({ stores })` declares a `[[vectorize]]` binding; without `indexName`, add it to `wrangler.toml` yourself. `miu deploy cloudflare` writes both. Workers AI and Vectorize exist only on Cloudflare; locally use `anthropic()` or `openaiCompatible()` with `memoryVectors()` or `sqliteVectors(db)`. `sqliteVectors(d1("DB"))` from `@miujs/db` resolves the D1 binding per request.
